:::{#exm-equivalence-relation}
#### Integers with an even difference

On the [integers](number-systems.qmd#def-integers),
define the [relation](functions.qmd#def-relation) $\sim$ by
$a \sim b$ when $a - b$ is [even](number-systems.qmd#def-even-odd).
For example, $7 \sim 3$, since $7 - 3 = 4 = 2 \cdot 2$,
but $7 \not\sim 4$, since $7 - 4 = 3$ is [odd](number-systems.qmd#def-odd).
The relation $\sim$ is an [equivalence relation](#def-equivalence-relation).

**[Reflexive](#def-reflexive).**
For every [integer](number-systems.qmd#def-integers) $a$, $a - a = 0 = 2 \cdot 0$, so $a \sim a$.

**[Symmetric](#def-symmetric-relation).**
Suppose $a \sim b$, so $a - b = 2k$ for some integer $k$.
Then

$$
\ba
b - a
&= -(a - b)
&& \text{(negate the difference)}
\\
&= -2k
&& \text{(} a - b = 2k \text{)}
\\
&= 2(-k),
&& \text{(factor out } 2 \text{)}
\ea
$$

and $-k$ is an integer, so $b \sim a$.

**[Transitive](algebra.qmd#def-transitive).**
Suppose $a \sim b$ and $b \sim c$,
so $a - b = 2j$ and $b - c = 2k$ for some integers $j$ and $k$.
Then

$$
\ba
a - c
&= (a - b) + (b - c)
&& \text{(the } b \text{ terms cancel)}
\\
&= 2j + 2k
&& \text{(} a - b = 2j \text{ and } b - c = 2k \text{)}
\\
&= 2(j + k),
&& \text{(distributive law)}
\ea
$$

and $j + k$ is an integer, so $a \sim c$.

:::
